methodology: The study employed a finite element analysis (FEA)-based numerical homogenization method to evaluate the effective thermo-mechanical properties of a large-scale additively manufactured short fiber-reinforced polymer composite using realistic periodic representative volume elements (RVEs) generated from reconstructed X-ray µ-CT images of a 3D-printed bead. Sensitivity analysis was performed on a single region of interest (ROI) extracted from the bead's volume to determine an appropriate RVE size.
research_objective: The main goal of the study was to numerically evaluate and predict the effective thermo-mechanical properties of large-scale additively manufactured short fiber-reinforced polymer composites, with a focus on understanding how inherent micro-porosities and spatial variation in the microstructure across the bead specimen affect these properties.

key_findings.finding: The Mori-Tanaka-Benveniste analytical estimates for effective properties were found to be comparable with numerical results.
Inherent micro-porosities reduced the composite's effective properties.
Numerical boundary value problem (BVP) full-field methods, mainly finite element analysis (FEA)-based homogenization methods have emerged for computing effective properties of SFRP composites.
Numerical-based methods prevail in terms of accuracy over analytical-based methods when predicting properties of composites with high aspect ratio and high volume fraction inclusions.

Effective thermo-mechanical properties computed from numerical homogenization scheme agree reasonably well with analytical mean-field homogenization approach based on Mori-Tanaka-Benveniste formulation, especially for low fiber aspect ratios and small phase property contrasts.
The influence of porosity (presence of micro-voids) on effective properties is also quantified.
Correlation study between effective thermo-mechanical properties and microstructural properties across regions of interest (ROIs) in LAAM-printed beads.
